04 / DESIGN

A class should feel
like an invitation.

A teacher with personality, an activity worth trying, and a result that belongs to the student. Art makes each step understandable.

THE CORE LOOP

  1. 01

    Discover

    A distinctive teacher and place make the subject inviting.

  2. 02

    Experiment

    Try a simple idea with an immediate, readable consequence.

  3. 03

    Revise

    Helpful feedback gives the next attempt a purpose.

  4. 04

    Express

    Perform or display what you made. See a reason to return.

FIRST MUSIC CLASS

Listen. Try.
Make it yours.

A proposed 2–3 minute experience: meet the Goblin, hear a four-beat phrase, identify the rest, and build a variation. End by performing the phrase and seeing a small completion moment.

Try the interaction sketch →

Art does the teaching, too.

WHO TO APPROACH
A clear silhouette, open gesture and unmistakable instrument.
WHAT TO TOUCH
A consistent selection cue and a focused teaching surface.
WHAT CHANGED
Sound, beat pulse and a persistent visible state.
HOW TO CONTINUE
A short prompt and a teacher who leaves space for a response.

ACCESS & SCOPE

Room to try.
Room to belong.

Pair voice with text. Let the student replay or mute it. Pair color with symbols. Use discrete choices before demanding precise rhythm timing.

The first slice uses one corner, one teacher and a short activity. Social classes, a wider campus and live AI conversation are future ideas. The current sketch has not established learning efficacy.

Desktop web first. Immersive Meta Quest work follows with controller input, comfortable viewing and real headset testing.
